about.title: about
about.paragraph_1: the video art explores personal and social barriers—the boundaries people construct or that society imposes from outside. switching television channels becomes the central metaphor: the viewer seems to peer into different flats in one building, watching fragments of other lives filled with inner conflicts, failures, and attempts to connect with the world.
about.paragraph_2: each scene is a separate “flat,” a separate life where a struggle unfolds for control over one’s body and identity, a confrontation with imposed social attitudes, and absurd, doomed attempts at communication. the viewer becomes an accidental witness, switching channels and observing barriers in other people’s lives.
about.paragraph_3: edited like rapid channel switching using stop motion, the sequence directly references the phenomenon of clip thinking. beat-driven music, with its recurring loops and insistent riffs, is its sonic equivalent. it does not develop according to classical rules but cycles endlessly, producing an effect similar to infinite scrolling on social media. each track was composed specifically for a separate theme of the video art.

implicit_attitudes.title: topic no. 1. implicit attitudes
implicit_attitudes.text: The topic of “implicit attitudes” reveals the deconstruction of unconscious stereotypes which, as an invisible framework of human thought, systematically distort the perception of social reality and reproduce inequality.

body_biopolitics.title: topic no. 2. biopolitics of the body
body_biopolitics.text: The topic of the “biopolitics of the body” examines how contemporary power subordinates and regulates human physical existence through medicine, law, and social norms, turning life into an object of governance.

communication_dysfunction.title: topic no. 3. communication dysfunction
communication_dysfunction.text: “Communication dysfunction” often appears as a persistent inability to establish open dialogue. people’s chronic inability to reach agreement arises not so much from differences of opinion as from a fundamental unwillingness to recognise the legitimacy of another person’s feelings and experience.
